Journal

JUR-nuhl · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Journal is a written record kept regularly, or a magazine on a particular subject.

Every summer, Tessa writes about her camping trips in her journal.

Worked Example

The scientist kept a journal, noting what her plants looked like each morning.

She writes her notes regularly, morning after morning. A written record you keep like that is a journal.

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

How Strong Is It? — Note → journal → Chronicle

Note vs. journal

Note vs. journal: A note is tiny: one quick message on a sticky pad.

Chronicle vs. journal

Chronicle vs. journal: A chronicle is bigger: a long, detailed record that can cover many years.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — journ

root — journ: day (French/Latin (jour, diurnus))

suffix — al

suffix — al: the act or result of (builds a noun here) (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Journ- means day, and here -al builds a noun: a journal is a day-by-day record of what happens.

Use the root in a new word: journey

Use the root in a new word: journey: The pioneers' journey west took many months - and long ago, a journey meant one day's travel, from the same root as journal!
